Map.reportMethodTitle: Criteria, weights and settings: ELECTRE TRI-B
Map.reportMethodIntro: The ELECTRE TRI-B method sorts alternatives (municipalities) into predefined categories by comparing them with reference profiles (thresholds). The parameters below control how sensitive the model is to differences between criterion values.
Map.reportDirectionNote: Benefit: the higher the value, the better the municipality is doing, lowering the priority for intervention. Cost: the higher the value, the worse the situation, raising the priority for intervention.
Map.reportIndifferenceDescription: Difference below which two values are considered equal
Map.reportPreferenceDescription: Difference from which a criterion is strictly preferred
Map.reportVetoDescription: Difference that cancels an alternative's dominance
Map.reportScenarioPessimisticNote: ELECTRE TRI-B produces two assignment procedures, optimistic and pessimistic, which may disagree when a municipality lies on the boundary between two classes. This analysis used the pessimistic scenario, assigning the municipality to the higher-priority class of the two when there is ambiguity. This is the more conservative choice, suited to public policy contexts where underestimating a territory's priority should be avoided.
Map.reportScenarioOptimisticNote: ELECTRE TRI-B produces two assignment procedures, optimistic and pessimistic, which may disagree when a municipality lies on the boundary between two classes. This analysis used the optimistic scenario, assigning the municipality to the lower-priority class of the two when there is ambiguity. This choice keeps the higher classes for territories whose priority is beyond doubt.
Map.reportNoExcluded: No municipality was excluded for missing data.
